package_info.why_malicious: The package was crafted to exploit a path traversal (ZIP Slip) vulnerability in the CDNJS automated ingestion pipeline, allowing arbitrary file write and potential remote code execution on the CDN infrastructure. This could lead to compromise of the CDN, exposure of secret API keys, and tampering with any library served by CDNJS.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when CDNJS bot fetches and unpacks new npm package releases)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The tarball contains files with directory traversal sequences in their paths, designed to escape the intended extraction directory and write files to arbitrary locations on the server filesystem.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of directory traversal (../../) in archive file paths is a classic indicator of a ZIP Slip/path traversal exploit, aiming to overwrite or create files outside the intended extraction directory.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should only contain files within their own directory structure. This package attempts to write to /tmp or other arbitrary locations, violating package isolation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate npm package should use directory traversal in archive paths; this is always suspicious.
key_indicators: Archive entries with ../../ in their paths
Files extracted outside the package root

execution_context.trigger: runtime (if the extracted shell script is executed by the system or by a follow-up process)
required_permissions: potentially environment_vars if script is executed

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This is a benign proof-of-concept shell script, but in a real attack, this file could contain arbitrary malicious code to be executed on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The presence of a shell script written to an arbitrary location via path traversal is highly suspicious, as it could be used for code execution or persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should not write or execute arbitrary shell scripts outside their own directory.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None in the context of npm packages distributed via public registries.
key_indicators: Shell script written outside package directory

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious npm package (hey-sven) containing files with directory traversal paths.
attack_chain.leads_to: CDNJS bot fetches and unpacks the package.

attack_chain.action: CDNJS automated ingestion bot unpacks the npm tarball, extracting files to unintended locations on the server due to path traversal.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary files (e.g., shell scripts) are written to sensitive locations.

attack_chain.action: Extracted files (e.g., /tmp/ryotak.sh) could be executed, or sensitive files could be overwritten or exfiltrated.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential remote code execution or leakage of secrets.

attack_chain.action: Sensitive API keys and secrets are exposed at public CDN URLs due to overwritten files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains write access to CDNJS infrastructure, enabling tampering with any library or the CDN itself.

behavioral_signatures: Archive extraction with directory traversal (../../) in file paths
Unexpected files appearing outside intended extraction directories
Automated ingestion pipelines extracting npm/tar archives without path sanitization
file_indicators: npm package tarballs containing entries with ../../ in their paths
Unexpected shell scripts or files in /tmp or other sensitive directories after package ingestion
network_indicators: Unusual access to CDNJS ingestion endpoints from new npm packages
Public URLs serving unexpected or sensitive content (e.g., API keys, scripts not belonging to the library)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages containing archive entries with directory traversal sequences (../../). Implement strict path sanitization during archive extraction in automated ingestion pipelines. Alert on the appearance of unexpected files or scripts in sensitive directories after package ingestion. Scan public CDN URLs for exposure of secrets or files not belonging to the intended library.
